messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High 5xx rate detected for service 'inference-api' in eu-west-1. 5xx rate > 10% over 3m. Trigger: error_rate_threshold_v2. thread created.
Maria Gonzalez: seeing spike from ~12:03 UTC, dashboards show ELB 5xx and target health failing in multiple AZs.
Liam Chen: paging @oncall - I'm on call. initial triage: is this an app regression or infra?
Alex Patel: quick grep of logs shows backend returning 502 from upstreams intermittently; ELB access logs show high 502/503s and target health failing. not code deploy related AFAICT.
Carol Nguyen: AWS Health API - any confirmation? @AWSStatusBot can you share official notice if there is one.
AWSStatusBot: official: "Investigating: Intermittent network connectivity issues impacting EC2 and ELB in eu-west-1 (Dublin)." See: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incident/eu-west-1/network/2026/03/15
Maria Gonzalez: customers affected: hosted API endpoints in eu-west-1 and several Dedicated nodes provisioned in eu-west-1. Observed ENI RX drops and TCP resets at instance level.
Raj Srivastava: ELB logs snippet sample:
```
201 2026-03-15T12:04:01Z app/my-inference-elb 10.0.1.2:443 172.31.0.4:8080 0.000 0.123 0.001 502
```
Liam Chen: runbook step1: set routing fallback to nearest healthy region. Plan: shift weight off eu-west-1 to eu-central-1 at 30% initial to test behavior.
Maria Gonzalez: executing Route53 change: updating weights for inference.example.com -> eu-central-1:30, eu-west-1:70 (will watch for failover errors).
Alex Patel: also enabling cross-zone load balancing on the ALBs and increasing ELB idle timeout to 120s per runbook to reduce connection churn.
Carol Nguyen: opening AWS support case (1234567890) now and requesting expedite due to customer impact. tagging TAM.
Liam Chen: rolling emergency page to networking and infra: @Raj can you escalate with AWS and request ENI / control plane health metrics? we need their internal RCA if it's control plane related.
Raj Srivastava: on it. collecting ENA/ENA driver errors, instance-level dmesg and kernel logs. creating a secure channel with AWS support.
Maria Gonzalez: early impact estimate: ~12% of total EU traffic returning 5xx; several enterprise Dedicated customers hosted in eu-west-1 report near 100% failure (private routing). prepping customer comms.
Alex Patel: mitigation attempt: draining targets in az-1 and az-2 to isolate flapping hosts. Note: draining increased retry pressure and caused downstream 429 spikes, rolled back drain after 3m.
Liam Chen: rolled config: enabling connection-level retries and client-side backoff for the gateway to reduce bursts while we keep routes shifting.
Carol Nguyen: public status draft (DO NOT SEND until reviewed): "We are investigating network issues in eu-west-1 impacting API request success. Traffic is being rerouted to healthy regions and we are working with AWS. Updates every 30 minutes."
Maria Gonzalez: +1 to send now. add note about potential increased latency for EU customers and that some Dedicated customers may see degraded service.
IncidentBot: Incident created: incident_id=INC-20260315-42 severity=sev2. Incident manager: Liam Chen. Handoff channel: #incidents.
Liam Chen: assigning tasks: Maria - customer comms & status page, Alex - traffic routing & ALB configs, Raj - AWS liaison & logs, Carol - postmortem owner and timeline.
Carol Nguyen: quick handoff: I'm on call til 14:00 UTC then Liam will take full command; Liam confirm?
Liam Chen: I'll take full command at 14:00 UTC - noted. Current mitigation: Route53 weights adjusted -> monitoring 5xx trend and latency.
AWSStatusBot: update: "AWS detected partial control plane issue in eu-west-1 causing ELB target health flapping. Engineers deploying mitigations; customers may see reduced availability in affected subnets."
Maria Gonzalez: customer update sent to enterprise customers via email and in-console banner: "We are mitigating a regional networking issue affecting inference responses in EU. We will provide updates every 30 minutes."
Alex Patel: after initial weight shift, 5xx dropped from ~12% -> ~4% over 20 minutes. Failover traffic shows +180ms latency for routed requests.
Raj Srivastava: AWS requested that we failover critical Dedicated clusters to eu-central-1 for affected customers. This requires product approval for temporary data locality change.
Carol Nguyen: quick poll in thread: objections to emergency failover for impacted Dedicated customers? product_signoff: none. Approving emergency migration for availability.
Liam Chen: approved, begin cross-region failover for two Dedicated clusters (runbook step 6). Notifying customers of brief maintenance window and potential latency increase.
Maria Gonzalez: updating status page and posting clear timeline. Next update scheduled in 20 minutes.
(Later)
IncidentBot: checkpoint 30m: mitigation in progress. Current metrics: residual 5xx ~2%, latency elevated for failover traffic. Incident remains sev2. Continue monitoring and collect artifacts for postmortem.
Liam Chen: thanks team. Carol, Raj, Alex — please snapshot all config changes, Route53 diffs, AWS case notes, and ELB logs. Handoff to next oncall: @Liam remains primary until 16:00 UTC.
Carol Nguyen: acknowledged. I'll own the postmortem and timeline. :pencil2: compiling actions and timestamps.
Maria Gonzalez: final ops note: affected Dedicated customers should be offered usage credits and private technical debriefs. I'll assemble impacted-customer list and send to CS.
Liam Chen: closing loop for now — keep monitoring and flag any regression. We'll run a full postmortem once AWS confirms root cause and we have timelines.
